question: Which patriarch am I?
reference: Genesis 12-22 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Abraham')

clues: God told me to leave my country and my father's household for a land he would show me.
I was promised descendants as countless as the stars, though my wife was past childbearing.
I pleaded with God to spare a wicked city if even ten righteous people were found in it.
I was stopped at the last moment from sacrificing my son on a mountain.

question: Which tax collector am I?
reference: Luke 19:1-10 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Zacchaeus', p. 1218)

clues: I was a chief tax collector in Jericho, and wealthy.
I was short, so I climbed a sycamore-fig tree to see Jesus pass.
Jesus called me down by name and said he would stay at my house.
I promised to give half my goods to the poor and repay any fraud fourfold.

question: Which fisherman apostle am I?
reference: John 1:40-42; 6:8-9 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Andrew')

clues: I was a fisherman and first a disciple of John the Baptist.
I brought my more famous brother to meet Jesus.
At the feeding miracle, I pointed out a boy with five loaves and two fish.
Tradition says I was later put to death on a cross of an unusual shape.

question: Which court prophet am I?
reference: 2 Samuel 7; 12; 1 Kings 1 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Nathan No. 2')

clues: I served in the royal court during the reign of King David.
I told the king he would not build God's house, but his son would.
I confronted him with a story about a rich man who stole a poor man's only lamb.
Later I helped make sure Solomon, not Adonijah, was made king.

question: Which wife of David am I?
reference: 1 Samuel 25 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Abigail No. 1')

clues: I was married to a harsh, foolish man named Nabal.
My husband insulted David's men after they had protected his flocks.
I rode out with food and calmed David before he shed blood in anger.
After Nabal died, I became one of David's wives.

question: Which contemporary of Isaiah am I?
reference: Micah 5:2; 6:8 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Micah No. 1')

clues: I prophesied in Judah in the days of kings Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.
I foretold that a ruler of Israel would come out of Bethlehem Ephrathah.
I summed up what God requires as doing justice, loving kindness, and walking humbly with God.
Jeremiah's defenders once quoted me to save his life.

question: Which priest-king am I?
reference: Genesis 14:18-20; Hebrews 7 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Melchizedek')

clues: I was both king of Salem and a priest of the Most High God.
I brought out bread and wine to a returning warrior and blessed him.
Abraham gave me a tenth of everything.
Hebrews says my priesthood pictures that of the Messiah.

question: Which member of the ruling council am I?
reference: John 3; 7:50; 19:39 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Nicodemus')

clues: I was a Pharisee and a member of the Jewish ruling council.
I came to Jesus at night to ask about his teaching.
He told me a person must be born again to see the Kingdom of God.
After the crucifixion I brought about a hundred pounds of spices for his burial.

question: Which woman of the early Christian congregation am I?
reference: Acts 16:14-15 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Lydia No. 2')

clues: I was a seller of purple cloth from the city of Thyatira.
I worshipped God and met Paul at a riverside place of prayer near Philippi.
The Lord opened my heart to pay attention to what Paul was saying.
After my household and I were baptized, I urged the missionaries to stay in my home.

question: Which king of Judah am I?
reference: 2 Kings 22-23 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Josiah')

clues: I became king at the age of eight.
During repairs on the temple, the book of the Law was found and read to me.
I tore my garments and led a sweeping campaign against idolatry.
I was killed in battle against Pharaoh Necho at Megiddo.

question: Which disciple am I?
reference: Matthew 9:9; 10:3 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Matthew', p. 352)

clues: I was also known by the name Levi.
Jesus found me sitting at the tax collector's booth and said, Follow me.
I gave a great reception at my house, and Pharisees complained about the guests.
I wrote the Gospel account that opens the Christian Greek Scriptures.

question: Which old worship site am I?
reference: Genesis 28; 1 Kings 12 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Bethel No. 1')

clues: Jacob slept here with a stone for a pillow and dreamed of a stairway to heaven.
He named me house of God after that dream.
Centuries later, Jeroboam set up one of two golden calves here.
The prophet Amos was told to stop prophesying at my sanctuary.

question: Which port city of Asia am I?
reference: Acts 19 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Ephesus')

clues: I was a great port city of the Roman province of Asia.
Paul taught daily in the school of Tyrannus here for about two years.
Practitioners of magic burned their scrolls after seeing God's power.
A silversmith started a riot in my theater, shouting that Artemis was great.

question: Which prophet's servant am I?
reference: 2 Kings 5:20-27 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Gehazi')

clues: I was the attendant of a well-known prophet.
My master refused any payment from a healed Syrian commander.
I ran after the commander and lied to get silver and clothing for myself.
As punishment, the leprosy that had left Naaman clung to me.

question: Which last of the prophets am I?
reference: Malachi 1-4 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Malachi, Book Of', p. 298)

clues: My name means my messenger, and my book is the last of the Hebrew Scriptures.
I rebuked the priests for offering blind and lame animals in sacrifice.
I challenged the people to test God by bringing the full tithe.
I foretold a messenger who would prepare the way, and the coming of Elijah.

question: Which son of David am I?
reference: 2 Samuel 14-18 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Absalom')

clues: I was noted for my good looks and my very heavy head of hair.
I killed my half brother Amnon and then fled for three years.
I stood at the city gate stealing the hearts of the people from my father.
During my revolt I was caught by my head in an oak and killed by Joab.
